summary: Section 101 of the Companies Act, 2013 explains how a company must call a general meeting by giving proper notice. It requires at least twenty-one clear days of notice in writing or through electronic mode. However, a meeting can happen with a shorter notice if the required majority of members agree.
points: A general meeting requires at least twenty-one clear days of notice in writing or through electronic mode.
An annual general meeting can have a shorter notice if ninety-five percent of members entitled to vote agree.
Other general meetings can have a shorter notice if a majority of members holding ninety-five percent of voting share capital agree.
Every meeting notice must state the place, date, day, hour, and the business to be done.
Notices must be sent to all members, legal representatives, auditors, and directors.
An accidental failure to give notice or failure to receive it will not cancel the meeting proceedings.
example: Nova Enterprises Private Limited wants to hold its annual general meeting. Normally, the company must give a notice of at least twenty-one clear days to everyone. However, the directors realize they need to pass an urgent resolution sooner. They ask the shareholders for consent to hold the meeting on a shorter notice. Since ninety-five percent of the members entitled to vote agree to this in writing, Nova Enterprises Private Limited lawfully proceeds with the meeting without waiting for the full twenty-one days.

terms.meaning: A formal gathering of a company's shareholders or members to discuss and decide on company business.
An official appointed to examine and check the financial records of the company.

watch: An accidental omission to send notice does not make the meeting illegal.
